subject: Renewal proposal — VelociTech 2028 commit & price-stability
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@velocitech.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal — VelociTech 2028 commit & price-stability

Hi Elena — great talking this morning. Attached is the term sheet v3 reflecting the options we discussed: a 12‑month renewal with two paths: a conservative retainer + optional on-demand burst, or a committed embed (30% lower per‑token rate) with a 30% minimum uplift vs current retainer.

Key asks from VelociTech we included:
- 6‑month price hold for current SKU if you lock before 3/31
- Tiered credits for ramp months 1–3 if usage exceeds forecast

I pulled usage history for your account and included a suggested commit cadence in the sheet. Jonas (solutions) is copied to confirm performance and latency footprint on the committed variant.

Next step: if the commit path looks good, I can put together a DocuSign with the exact numbers and credit schedule. Otherwise we can finalize the retainer amendment.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 415‑555‑0192

Attachments: Redwood_VelociTech_Renewal_Termsheet_v3.pdf, Usage_History_Q1-2028.csv

From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@velocitech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@velocitech.com>
Date: 2028-03-11T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — VelociTech 2028 commit & price-stability

Thanks Ben — quick notes after reviewing the sheet: we appreciate the two-path approach. A couple of asks from procurement/CFO: 

1) Can Redwood extend the price hold to 9 months instead of 6 if we commit now? That reduces near-term budget unpredictability for us.
2) We need a capped true‑up for Q1 if our usage spikes — prefer a credit lane rather than a bill shock.
3) If we do the committed embed, CFO wants the commit reduced to a 20% uplift (vs 30% suggested) but with a stricter SLA and a formal credit for missed latency SLOs.

Happy to hop on a short call this week to align.

– Elena
VP Product, VelociTech
Elena.Martinez@velocitech.com

On 2028-03-11 09:12, Ben Carter wrote:
> Hi Elena — great talking this morning. Attached is the term sheet v3 reflecting the options we discussed...

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal — VelociTech 2028 commit & price-stability

Forwarding VelociTech's initial feedback. Elena is asking for a longer price hold (9 months) and a smaller uplift (20%) if we do a committed embed, but wants stronger SLA credits. Please draft two short options we can present:

Option A — 9‑month price hold + retainer (no embed) with tiered ramp credits for Q1 overage;
Option B — Commit at 20% uplift with increased SLO credit (dollars back on missed p95) and a capped true‑up mechanism.

Jonas: confirm any technical constraints on offering a stricter SLA for the committed model (esp p95 latency and availability windows).
Marissa: would you run this as a deal desk review? If we accept Option B we’ll need a margin check and exec approval for the adjusted pricing.

Thanks — keep it tight, they want to close before month-end.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Success & Renewals, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachments: SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-12T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal — VelociTech 2028 commit & price-stability

Irene — quick tech read: we can support a tightened SLA on the committed embed if we require a dedicated pool allocation and a short onboarding window to validate tail latencies. Impact notes:
- Dedicated slice = small incremental infra cost (we can cover via margin if deal economics allow).
- p95/availability credit scheme: recommend dollar credits tied to monthly MTTDL and p95 > threshold, capped at 15% of monthly invoice.
- Implementation: 2–3 week validation window; no impact to VelociTech's current integrations.

If Sales wants to offer a 9‑month price hold + 20% uplift commit, I recommend we tie the extra SLA commitments to the dedicated pool so we can guarantee performance.

— Jonas
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-13T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal — VelociTech 2028 commit & price-stability

Internal decision: we can greenlight Option B (20% uplift commit + dedicated pool + SLA credit) on the condition that VelociTech increases the commit baseline by 25% vs their current retainer and signs a 12‑month term. Margin delta acceptable if we treat the dedicated pool infra as capitalized over the term.

Ben — prepare a redline to the term sheet with:
- Commit: +25% baseline (32% uplift vs current throughput numbers), price = 20% off list for committed usage;
- Price hold: 9 months on legacy SKUs for any remaining retainer consumption;
- SLA: dollar credit for monthly p95 miss, capped at 15% monthly invoice; automatic fallback to retainer pool if dedicated slice unavailable;
- Credits: tiered ramp credits months 1–3 as proposed.

Once you have the redline, loop in Legal for standard commit language and get Marissa's sign-off for final. We should aim to send to VelociTech by EOD Thursday.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@velocitech.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@velocitech.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Updated terms for VelociTech renewal — committed embed option

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear feedback and time on the call. Attached is the redlined term sheet that reflects the deal team decision:

Summary of agreed commercial points:
- Commit path: 12‑month term, committed usage priced at 20% below list (applies to embedded tokens only).
- Commit baseline: 25% uplift on your existing retainer baseline (gives us runway to guarantee dedicated capacity).
- Price hold: 9 months for any remaining retainer SKUs; after the hold, pricing reverts to the agreed committed rates.
- SLA credit: dollar credits for missed p95 thresholds, capped at 15% of the affected month's invoice.
- Ramp credits: month 1–3 protective credits to cap true‑up exposure.

Next steps: I’ve included a DocuSign link for the term sheet; please review and sign if agreeable. Jonas will coordinate a 2‑week validation window for the dedicated pool once the contract is countersigned.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdef-123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/VEL-2028-049

Thanks — aiming to close by 3/31 as discussed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_VelociTech_Renewal_Termsheet_v3.pdf

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@velocitech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@velocitech.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Updated terms for VelociTech renewal — committed embed option

Ben — thanks, Elena and I reviewed the redline. This aligns with our internal constraints; we will route to legal and CFO for sign-off today. One clarifying question: the SLA credit cap of 15%—can you confirm how that interacts with month‑over‑month usage variability? We want to understand whether credits apply proportionally to committed usage only or to total invoice.

If you can confirm that quickly we’ll push the DocuSign internally and aim to return an executed copy within 48 hours.

— Rajiv Singh
Head of Procurement, VelociTech
